transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I’m here because I keep forgetting things I’m supposed to follow up on—scheduled callbacks, work orders, things I told people I’d handle. It’s gotten backed up so badly that work told me I need to come in before I mess up my chance at moving up.
Are you also forgetting things in your personal life, outside of work?

Yes, it’s not just at work. I’ll tell someone I’m going to call them back or take care of something, and then it just slips until it’s already piled up. That’s basically what brought me in—forgetting callbacks, work orders, follow-ups I said I’d handle. It’s gotten bad enough that my job sent me here before it costs me a chance to move up.
Do you find yourself getting distracted easily when you're supposed to be focusing on something?

Yes. Like I’ll open a digital work order and think I’m following it, but halfway through reading the notes my mind jumps to some other noise or the next job. Then I look back and realize I don’t even know what I just read.
Do you have trouble remembering things that happened recently?
I’m not really sure. I notice more that I forget what I was supposed to do, but remembering actual recent events… I haven’t paid much attention to that.
Can you recall what you did yesterday?
I can remember some of it, but not clearly start to finish. I know I went through my usual day, but if you want the details in order, I’d have to really think about it.
Have you noticed any significant decline in your ability to learn new things?

I’m not sure I’d call it a significant decline. I haven’t really noticed that I can’t learn new things, exactly. I might need things explained more than once sometimes, but I don’t know if that’s worse than before.
Do you ever feel confused or disoriented, like you're not sure what's going on around you?
No, not really. I don’t think I get confused about where I am or what’s happening around me. I might have to pause and think sometimes, but I wouldn’t call it disoriented.
Do you often find yourself struggling to find the right words when you're trying to express something?
Not really, no. I mean, sometimes I pause for a second if I’m tired or trying to explain something, but I don’t feel like I’m often stuck looking for words.
Do you have trouble remembering things from your past, like important events or people's names?
I don’t think so. I mean, I remember important things from my past and people’s names pretty normally, as far as I can tell. Nothing that feels unusual or like a big problem.
Do you feel like your memory or attention problems are interfering with your daily activities or relationships?

Yes. It’s become a real problem at work. I’ve got a backlog now, tenants have complained, and I even have a safety review on my record. I’m worried it’s going to mess up the promotion path I’ve been trying to work toward.
Have you noticed any changes in your mood lately?
I’m not really sure. I mean, I’ve been stressed, but I haven’t noticed a major change in my mood or anything like that.
Do you think your ability to remember and focus has gotten worse over time?

Yes, I think it has gotten worse. It’s been really noticeable for about 11 months now, since the new management company switched us over to digital work orders and made the documentation stricter. That’s when I really started having a harder time keeping up and staying focused.
Do you have trouble planning and organizing your tasks and daily activities?
I’m not sure how to answer that. I mean, I get through the day, but I haven’t really thought about whether it’s planning and organizing specifically. Could you maybe explain what you mean by that?
Do you think your memory or focus problems started after something specific happened or changed in your life?

Yes. It really became noticeable after the new management company took over and switched us to digital work orders. They also got stricter about the documentation, and since then—about 11 months ago—I’ve had a much harder time with my focus and keeping track of things.
Have you been diagnosed with any medical conditions or taken any new medications around the time your focus and memory problems started?
No, not that I can think of. I wasn’t diagnosed with anything new, and I don’t remember starting any new medication around that time.
Have you experienced any kind of traumatic event or severe stress around 11 months ago, when your focus and memory problems started?

I don’t think so. Nothing traumatic happened that I can point to. The main thing I remember changing around then was the job situation and the new system, but not like a specific major event or anything.
Do you find that your ability to focus and remember things gets worse as the day goes on?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t noticed a clear pattern where it definitely gets worse later in the day. Some days feel bad from the start, and other times it just depends on what I’m doing.
Have you experienced any numbness, tingling, or weakness in your arms or legs?
No, I haven’t really noticed any numbness or tingling. I don’t think I’ve had weakness in my arms or legs either.
Have you noticed any decline in your ability to perform daily tasks that require thinking, such as managing finances or cooking?

Yeah, mostly at work. I keep forgetting scheduled callbacks, work orders, and basic follow-ups I told people I’d do. It’s gotten piled up enough that they sent me here before I lose my chance at moving up.
Did the switch to digital work orders and stricter documentation at your job around 11 months ago cause any other significant changes in your daily routine or work environment?

Yeah, that’s about when it really started standing out. Since they switched us over to the digital work orders and got stricter about documenting everything, it’s been noticeably worse for me — about 11 months now.
